chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Basir asked him (the Imam), while I was present, about one who enters into ihram for Umrah during the months of Hajj, asking if he may return (home). He said: There is no Umrah in the months of Hajj where one returns to his family, but he is detained in Mecca until he completes his Hajj, because he only entered into ihram for that purpose.

Thus, this report clarifies that it was not permissible for him to do so, because he entered into ihram for Hajj, and this applies only to one who intends Tamattu' (combining) Umrah with Hajj, as we have explained.

key_terms.أَشْهُرُ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and first 10 days of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.تَمَتُّعٌ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj under one ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who performs Umrah in the Hajj months and wants to return home before Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the ruling of Umrat al-Tamattu', where a pilgrim entering Mecca during the Hajj months with the intention of combining Umrah and Hajj must remain in Mecca (Ihtibat) after completing Umrah until Hajj begins. It distinguishes this from Umrat al-Qiran or individual Umrah, emphasizing that the initial ihram was specifically for the combined ritual, thus preventing the pilgrim from returning home prematurely. This ruling underscores the structural integrity of the Tamattu' form of Hajj in Shia jurisprudence.
